settings.dev_machines.allow_docker_desc: Each new machine gets its own sandboxed Docker daemon, so people and agents can run docker compose (builds, volumes, any number of services). Containers reach the Internet only through the machine's egress proxy. Turning it off stops machines that have a daemon from starting.
settings.dev_machines.allow_sudo_desc: People can run sudo in the terminal and IDE of each new machine, for example to install system packages with apt. Agent attempts always run without sudo. Global npm installs, such as updating Claude Code with npm i -g, work without sudo and are kept on the machine's workspace.
settings.dev_machines.allow_sudo_warning: Sudo gives machine users root inside their containers

The terminal and IDE containers of new machines get a writable system filesystem and can gain root privileges. They stay on the machine network: Internet access still goes through the egress proxy, root cannot change the machine's network settings, and nothing from the host is mounted. System changes are lost when a container is recreated; only /workspace is kept. Machines created with sudo cannot start after you turn it off.
